example.title: Show it with a chair
example.prompt: “How confident do you feel about the upcoming math test? Show me through how you interact with your chair!”

options.label: Under
options.line: “Please don’t make me take this test!”

blocks.text: In Position Mapping, students answer a question without saying a word. They show how they feel through where they place their bodies in relation to an object. Close, far, on top, hiding behind: every position tells a story.
For example: let’s use chairs! Pose a question like:
“How confident do you feel about the upcoming math test? Show me through how you interact with your chair!”

items: Standing tall on the chair (safely!): “I’ve got this!”
Peeking out from behind it: “I’m a little nervous…”
Lying under it or walking away from it: “Please don’t make me take this test!”

blocks.text: Position Mapping gives every student a voice, including those who might not want to share their feelings out loud. In one glance, the teacher gets a quick, honest read of the whole class. Students also practise using their bodies and space to show emotion. Follow it up by inviting a few volunteers to explain their choice.
If climbing on chairs is a concern in your classroom, set a simple safety rule first, like “feet stay on the floor.”
